title: Foundry-lite Action Types v3 parity matrix
scope: Promote the single-object setProperty action executor into a general Ontology transaction + agent-native action platform (typed IR, multi-object/link atomic edit plan, function/batch edits, typed parameters/forms/sections/struct/media/attachment/criteria, governed side effects, scale and monitoring, action log, revert, branch/scenario, interface actions, SDK/API/UI and separate builder/consumer MCP distribution).

statusDefinitions.foundation: Base model or port exists, but no end-to-end runtime behavior.
statusDefinitions.partial: Some implementation exists but a required proof, surface, or live/E2E evidence is absent.
statusDefinitions.current: Implementation + repository/contract tests + live/E2E + SDK evidence all present.

reusedStrengths: ActionMutationUnitOfWork.commit (action_mutations.py:42) is a per-object commit primitive already looped over many objects by ActionBatchService inside one transaction.
CAS: update_object_target WHERE object_version==expected + object_records_version append; status_cas.cas_status_transition WHERE status IN from_statuses.
Transactional outbox + masked audit + run_relation via runtime_service evidence boundary.
safe_expression.py: eval-free precondition grammar with a robust hand-written tokenizer.
External-writeback three-phase before-commit saga (external_pending WAL, AMBIGUOUS-never-failure, reconcile) — the substrate for gating side effects.
OSDK resource-scope authorization (domain/platform/scopes.py + require_resource_scope) enforced across function/action/object services.
SDK codegen (scripts/sdk_generator/*) with a byte-exact --check drift gate wired into the static lane, plus check_frontend_backend_surface.py.
Real runtime hooks to connect to: FunctionExecutionService, interface conformance validation, ontology branch snapshot/proposal-merge.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: An action type is a typed set of rules (createObject, modifyObject(s), createOrModifyObject, deleteObject(s), createLink, deleteLink, function edit, interface variants) each with a stable identity and evaluation order; rule value sources are parameter, object-reference property, static, and contextual (current user / current timestamp).
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: action_types.definition JSON carries mutations[] limited to {type:'setProperty', property, value|valueFrom}; ACTION_MUTATION_TYPES=frozenset({'setProperty'}); valueFrom resolves only params.<key>.
capabilities.targetBehavior: A typed Action IR v2 with all rule kinds, stable ruleId + explicit order, and a validated value-expression AST covering every value source (no eval, no string interpolation). v1 setProperty definitions normalize to a v2 modifyObject rule at compile time (dual-read).
capabilities.remainingGap: The typed IR (all rule kinds + eval-free value-expression AST), ordering/exclusivity validation, and the v1->v2 normalizing compiler are complete and now consumed by the live apply path (commit ac0e2a05): a rulesV2 action authored in ontology YAML compiles and runs through foundry.actions.apply, proven by the FulfillOrder E2E. FunctionEditRule is parsed into the IR but its execution is deferred to function-backed-actions; prior-rule output as a value position (vs a link endpoint) and webhook/function value sources are deferred.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: Rules compile into a deterministic per-object edit; multiple rules touching the same property resolve by order; invalid orderings (delete-before-add, modify-before-add, double-create) fail at compile time; all edits commit atomically on submission.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: The 'plan' is an implicit list of setProperty patches; ActionMutationUnitOfWork commits one object; ActionBatchService loops it over same-type targets sharing one patch. No structured EditPlan object.
capabilities.targetBehavior: An immutable EditPlan (objectsToCreate/Modify/Delete, linksToCreate/Delete, readSetVersions, expectedWriteVersions, stableOperationKeys, originatingRuleIds, provenance, permission evidence, redacted parameter snapshot, sideEffectPlan) built, validated, then committed as a separate stage.
capabilities.remainingGap: The immutable EditPlan, whole-plan validator, ordered IR->plan builder, ActionEditPlanCommitter, and the live LivePlanResolutionContext adapter run end to end on the real apply path (commit ac0e2a05). Deferred: function-rule planning (raises today), prior-rule output as a property value, and objectSet resolution is minimal (list-of-ids).

capabilities.palantirBehavior: One action can create/modify/delete objects of multiple types and create/delete many-to-many links, committing all Ontology edits all-or-nothing; foreign-key (one-to-many) links are set by modifying the object's foreign-key property, not a link rule.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: ActionRepository exposes only update_object_target (CAS) + insert_object_edit (edit_type='set_property'); no object create/delete and no action-facing link create/delete. Single target_object_type is hard-coded.
capabilities.targetBehavior: A transactional committer that applies a heterogeneous EditPlan across object types and M:M links in one Postgres transaction with per-edit CAS, stable create IDs, link uniqueness/cardinality checks, dangling-link prevention, tenant guard, audit+outbox+idempotency, and stale-plan rejection.
capabilities.remainingGap: Live-proven and hardened: the FulfillOrder rulesV2 action modifies its target Order, creates a second Order, and links them in one transaction with read-your-writes, one action run + per-object edit rows, idempotent replay, action-role permission denial, and stale-version conflict rollback (commits ac0e2a05 + review fixes). An adversarial review then closed an OCC lost-update window (the target CAS now binds to the client-validated expectedObjectVersion) and a link-endpoint visibility hole (endpoints resolve through the same row/segment visibility check as modify/delete), with regression tests in test_action_plan_resolution.py; repository primitives are SQLite+PG contract-tested. Deferred deltas: per-object-type SEGMENT-mask edit-through enforcement (row visibility + action-level Apply are enforced), and external side effects on the v2 path (writeback/function rules).

capabilities.palantirBehavior: A function rule (mutually exclusive with all other rules) delegates all edits to an ontology edit function that returns a typed edit batch; the action engine applies it; the function itself never writes; function version is pinned.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: FunctionExecutionService runs a persisted Logic DAG, read/compute-only, gated on role + OSDK function:execute scope + input validation. It does not produce or apply an ontology edit batch.
capabilities.targetBehavior: A function rule whose result is a typed OntologyEditBatch re-validated (schema, existence, permissions, tenant, constraints, version, limits, sensitive-field policy) and applied only by the edit-plan committer, with function apiName/version pinned and deterministic operation keys.
capabilities.remainingGap: Current for the Action-Type function rule boundary: activation pins and type-checks the Logic DAG function contract; per-request mode executes at most 20 requests sequentially; batched mode invokes one list-of-struct input for up to 10,000 requests; a single Action call in batched mode is represented by a one-item list; all returned edits are combined, revalidated and committed once through the fenced Temporal run. The engine rejects more than 10,000 edits, more than 50 edited object types and inconsistent read sets before commit. API, TypeScript/Python SDK, Builder, browser and PostgreSQL+Temporal two-worker kill/takeover evidence are green. A general arbitrary Python/TypeScript Functions authoring and sandbox product is intentionally outside this Action Types capability, not an unproven requirement of this axis.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: Parameters are typed (string/boolean/integer/long/double/decimal/date/timestamp/object/objectSet/attachment/geohash/geoshape/mediaReference/marking/struct/array), individually form-exposed and editable, with static / object-property / type-class defaults; one canonical schema drives server validation, SDK, form, and MCP input schema.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: parameter_schema is a JSON-Schema subset; safe_expression validates required/unknown/typed params limited to string/integer/float/boolean; defaults are absent; the ActionFormPanel renders scalar inputs.
capabilities.targetBehavior: An extensible typed parameter schema with the full type set, defaults (static/object-property/type-class), and one canonical schema generating server validation + TS SDK + browser form + MCP tool input schema.
capabilities.remainingGap: The canonical contract now supports primitive/date/timestamp/decimal/object/interface/objectSet/array/struct/media/attachment parameters, deterministic defaults, deterministic section/column layout with typed visibility conditions, inline-eligibility metadata, JSON Schema, recursive server validation, deterministic MCP tool schema, and sectioned React runtime forms. Ontology activation and the FastAPI catalog preserve the complete canonical schema extensions instead of rebuilding or response-filtering them. The compiler exposes an inline cell binding only for one selected object, one editable property, one primitive parameter, no function and no effects; Object Explorer executes that binding through the same dynamic Action/OCC/idempotency path, with browser proof. The branch-first Builder authors scalar/reference/collection and nested struct parameters without raw JSON, while the runtime renders recursive struct controls and rejects invalid JSON before submission. The TypeScript and Python OSDK generators emit the same fingerprinted per-Action types. Media/attachment controls now upload before form submission, enforce size/format and canonical references, inherit object access, retain an append-only lifetime holder ledger, quarantine provisional uploads, scan before staging, persist redacted scan evidence, reject EICAR-classified input without storing bytes, and require a ClamAV profile in protected runtimes. Live ClamAV/PostgreSQL and a real external client remain unproven, so this stays partial.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: Conditional overrides modify a parameter's visibility/requiredness/default/constraints; first-matching block wins; conditions reference only parameters above in the form hierarchy.
capabilities.targetBehavior: Typed conditional overrides evaluated first-match-wins with an above-in-hierarchy reference constraint, shared with submission-criteria condition model.
capabilities.remainingGap: Current for the canonical override boundary. First-match overrides replace visibility, requiredness, default and the complete constraint set; only earlier parameters may be referenced. The same typed AST is compiled and validated server-side, round-trips through no-code Builder authoring and reload, generates deterministic SDK/form metadata, and is evaluated by the runtime before native input validation. Browser evidence proves first-match ordering, base-vs-override enum and length constraints, invalid override defaults blocking submit, conditional section visibility, and attachment requiredness changing from an earlier parameter.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: Submission criteria combine nestable ALL/ANY/NONE with comparison operators over parameters, object properties, linked-object attributes, and current-user identity/group/attributes; evaluated at submit; block submission with a per-condition failure message; independent of data permissions.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: safe_expression preconditions support only == 'literal' and in [list] over string-coerced values; no boolean composition, numeric comparison, negation, or user/group operands.
capabilities.targetBehavior: A typed Boolean submission-criteria AST (all/any/not; equals/notEquals/in/notIn/gt/gte/lt/lte/contains/matches/exists; parameter, object-property, current-user/group/attribute operands) evaluated server-side and generated for the client from one schema.
capabilities.remainingGap: Current for typed submission criteria. Nested all/any/not and the full typed comparison set operate over parameters, target properties, permission-scoped linked-object values/counts, current user id, groups and arbitrary verified IdP attributes. Header-trust development auth and OIDC both normalize attributes into RequestContext; async plans snapshot them for fenced revalidation without exposing hidden linked values. The Builder authors and reloads a linked Customer plus currentUser.department condition, the runtime renders the authoritative redacted per-clause decision, and browser evidence proves the correct identity succeeds while a different department is blocked. App restrictions, OAuth scopes and linked read-set drift remain fail-closed.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: Distinct View/Edit/Apply permissions; applying uses the submitting user's own permissions so an action cannot edit unseen objects/links; effective access is the intersection of user identity/role/group, object/link/action-type policy, OSDK app scope, and MCP scope; submission criteria are an independent gate.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: PolicyService RBAC with action:execute:<name> roles (fail-closed), object:read target guard, property masking (classification/segment), not-found masking (visible_record), segment_mutation_denied_error. OSDK resource-scope enforced for function/action.
capabilities.targetBehavior: The same intersection extended to every v2 edit: per-edited-object/link read+edit checks in the plan validator, function-execute and side-effect-execute permissions, sensitive-parameter and high-risk-approval gates, uniform not-found masking.
capabilities.remainingGap: Current evidence covers independent canonical viewRoles/editRoles/applyRoles with legacy allowedRoles dual-read, permission-filtered active and branch catalogs, branch mutation enforcement, actor access flags in the generated SDK, server-side Apply denial, per-edit object/link/property/function/connector checks, OSDK application and OAuth/MCP scope intersection, approval-time revalidation, and recipient-by-recipient notification filtering. Browser evidence authors the three grants, proves a data engineer can View/Edit but cannot Apply, proves missing app/token linked-resource grants fail, and proves an MCP high-risk request cannot self-approve. Notification policies resolve trusted current recipient roles and enforce strict or best-effort delivery against every affected object's read and row policy; recipient evidence is count/hash only.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: A single before-commit (gating) webhook runs before rule evaluation; if it fails no Ontology change is made; its output can feed subsequent rules.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: The external-writeback saga (external_pending WAL, receipt, outcome_unknown/compensation_required/reconciled) is the before-commit external-call substrate, but only an S3 adapter exists and the target URI is caller-supplied (not action-owned).
capabilities.targetBehavior: A before-commit gating webhook owned by the action definition (approved connector/resource only), whose durable receipt integrates the existing outcome_unknown/compensation_required/reconciliation paths and whose response fields are a rule value source.
capabilities.remainingGap: The target behavior is complete for this axis. A v3 Action owns one registered-connector before webhook; a durable fenced receipt is written before dispatch, SSRF and inline URI are blocked, known failure prevents commit, and ambiguous delivery closes outcome_unknown without replay. Builder-authored typed response fields feed declaration-only rule assignments; missing, undeclared, misplaced or wrong-typed responses fail before Ontology commit. Operator reconciliation is available through API, TypeScript/Python SDK and browser UI. A real PostgreSQL multi-process proof kills the first worker before and after remote dispatch: pre-dispatch work is safely taken over with an incremented fencing token and exactly one provider call, while post-dispatch ambiguity is never replayed and remains outcome_unknown until structured reconciliation evidence is supplied.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: Multiple after-commit side effects (webhook, notification, event, schedule/build trigger, connector command) fire after edits are applied, unordered, possibly async; their failure does not roll back the edits.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: action_types.definition carries sideEffects[] but no executor; the transactional outbox (at-least-once, lease reclaim, DLQ) delivers action.run.committed/object.changed only.
capabilities.targetBehavior: Action-owned after-commit side effects delivered via the outbox with stable idempotency keys, retry classification, bounded backoff, dead-letter/operator evidence, delivery receipts, secret redaction, and network policy; notifications rendered against pre-edit state.
capabilities.remainingGap: The target behavior is now complete for this axis. After-commit effects create transactionally paired outbox events and per-effect receipts, fan out concurrently without definition-order semantics, and route webhook, notification, event, schedule/build and connector-command kinds through governed connector or stream targets. Stable idempotency, classified retry/DLQ/outcome_unknown, lease takeover, fencing, connector/network/secret policy, tenant RLS, operator cancel/retry/reconciliation and no-code notification policies are active. Notification templates are validated at compile time and frozen from the target object's pre-edit version before the atomic Ontology commit; the receipt exposes only fingerprints and source-version evidence. Browser evidence covers authoring and operator controls. A real PostgreSQL multi-process proof kills the first worker before and after remote dispatch, proving exactly one provider call or fail-closed reconciliation instead of duplicate delivery. Vendor-specific notification template designers and provider packages remain product extensions rather than a gap in the canonical Action effect contract.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: An action submission is a durable, auditable unit with terminal and recovery states.
capabilities.targetBehavior: The existing state machine extended (validating/planned/queued/running/commit_pending as needed) for multi-object and asynchronous function/side-effect execution without duplicating states.
capabilities.remainingGap: The target behavior is complete for this axis. Durable queued/running/cancelling/commit_pending/terminal runs, steps, attempts, events, cancellation, lease takeover and fenced exact-one commit are live-proven with PostgreSQL, Temporal and two worker processes. The browser runtime shows run history, SSE reconnect with snapshot fallback, step/attempt/fencing, retry time, worker takeover, cancellation and terminal evidence. Monitoring uses a fixed 30-day UTC window, computes p95/failure/effect backlog, publishes threshold and minimum-sample policies, and enqueues active alerts once per policy and UTC hour. The Action control worker evaluates every tenant, the outbox preserves idempotency and audit evidence, and a real Kafka broker test proves external delivery. Typed adapter failures retry only safe timeout, unavailable and rate-limited classes; authorization, validation, conflict, unsupported, unknown, OOM, ambiguous outcome and reconciliation-required failures remain fail-closed.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: Each submission creates exactly one action log object foreign-key-linked to all edited objects, recording action RID/type/version, timestamp, user, edited object PKs, optional summary/parameter values; queryable via the Ontology, links, aggregations, and a timeline widget.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: action_log_entries creates one normalized [LOG] projection per successful v2/v3 submission and action_log_objects links every ordered object/link edit. Each enabled Action also projects a read-only virtual [LOG] <Action> Object Type into the active Ontology catalog and serves it through generic object get/filter/search/signed-cursor query/aggregation with definition, actor, redacted parameters, result, plan, approval, branch and effect-receipt evidence.
capabilities.targetBehavior: A durable action log (one record per submission) linked to every edited object/link, capturing full provenance, redacted parameters, side-effect receipts, and branch context, exposed as an Ontology-queryable read model.
capabilities.remainingGap: Current for the Action Log boundary. Every successful submission writes one normalized log and ordered edited-object links in the same transaction, exposed through API and generated SDK plus a virtual one-to-one [LOG] <Action> Object Type. Generic get, typed filter/search/order/signed-cursor pagination/aggregation and application-scope denial are DB-native; a 5,001-row regression rules out the old memory scan cap. The Ontology catalog now projects virtual [LOG LINK] Action::ObjectType links, generic link traversal applies both log and target-object permissions, and the runtime deep-links edited objects. The previously disconnected Workshop widget registry is now the published runtime path; browser evidence binds [LOG] to a real timeline and renders the committed run. PostgreSQL+Temporal live proof includes two-process concurrent revert with exactly one new winner log.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: Revert is allowed only if the edit is still the latest version, no later edit touched the object, the edit is reversible, and the caller has revert rights; it undoes object edits only, never side effects.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: Successful edits persist operation-specific inverse evidence; ActionLogRevertService checks the original actor, definition policy, latest edit, object version/deleted state and link state before applying all inverse object/link edits atomically.
capabilities.targetBehavior: A revert eligibility specification and service that restores object/link edits when still-latest and unconflicted, records a new action log, and never claims to undo already-emitted side effects (issuing a compensating action instead when needed).
capabilities.remainingGap: Current for safe Ontology revert. Eligibility requires the original actor, enabled version-pinned policy, latest object/link edit and unchanged state; inverse edits commit atomically and create a new non-revertible run/log/audit/outbox. Already-delivered external effects are explicitly preserved. Builder authors an optional distinct existing compensation Action, activation validates the reference, the execution-time policy is sealed in the immutable log, and runtime eligibility names the governed compensation path instead of pretending to reverse the provider. Browser evidence covers authoring, execution, evidence and revert; PostgreSQL+Temporal live evidence races two independent processes and proves one CAS winner, one winner log and complete two-object restoration while the same gate separately proves cancellation CAS.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: Actions can execute on a branch/scenario as an isolated edit overlay that never merges to main, with side effects suppressed by default and per-effect opt-in.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: OntologyBranchService provides isolated definition edits + proposal-merge, but actions are not executable against a branch overlay.
capabilities.targetBehavior: Branch/scenario action execution against an isolated edit overlay with dry-run/preview returning the redacted edit plan and impacted objects/links, conflict checks before merge, side effects suppressed by default, and a production action log after merge.
capabilities.remainingGap: Active or branch-only v3 Action definitions can plan and commit object plus link create/delete edits into tenant-scoped branch overlays without changing main. Object/link reads compose base+overlay, diff reports current-main drift, exact request replay is idempotent, effects are structurally suppressed, and repository contracts cover overlay CAS against SQLite and a real PostgreSQL container. The no-code browser journey now creates the Action on a branch, submits it as an Ontology proposal, has an assigned human reviewer approve it (the author may self-review), activates it, and immediately executes the dynamically discovered Action without SDK regeneration. It stays partial because non-production effect opt-in, a dedicated visual overlay-data diff/execution view, and a dedicated multi-process branch-overlay concurrency race are absent.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: Interface actions create a caller-selected concrete implementation, modify/delete through an interface reference, edit only shared interface properties, and create/delete links through interface link constraints. Create-link requires one concrete implementation while delete-link removes every matching implementation; primary keys remain immutable and every concrete type is re-validated.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: interface_types + query_by_interface + conformance validation exist; no interface-scoped action rules.
capabilities.targetBehavior: Interface-scoped create/modify/delete/link rules with typed references, shared-property-only edits, concrete create selection, link-constraint cardinality/target enforcement, and per-implementation permission/OCC validation.
capabilities.remainingGap: Interface-target Actions persist their target kind, accept typed object/interface references, select a concrete implementation at execution, create it only with expectedObjectVersion=0 and matching primary-key identity, bind modify/delete rules to that type, restrict assignments to shared properties, reject primary-key edits, and re-run concrete permissions plus OCC. Interface link constraints validate object/interface targets, cardinality and required implementation conformance; create-link requires exactly one concrete link while delete-link removes all matching implementations. The branch-first Builder authors these contracts and browser evidence verifies canonical serialization. Interface-target Actions and their derived [LOG] Object Types are discoverable through the Action/Ontology catalogs, and generated TypeScript/Python Action descriptors bind them to implementing object types while requiring the concrete type on unbound calls. It remains partial until production PostgreSQL concurrency evidence and the full branch proposal/activation browser journey pass.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: Actions are distributed through list/get, schema/form metadata, validate, plan/dry-run, apply, run get/list, events, cancel, action log, revert-eligibility, revert, and branch execution across API and typed SDK.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: 3 action routes (apply/apply-batch/validate); TS SDK generated from one ontology YAML with a byte-exact drift gate; Python OSDK hand-authored.
capabilities.targetBehavior: Extended action API + generated TS/Python SDK covering plan/dry-run, multi-object apply, run get/list, events, cancel, action log, revert, and branch execution, with SDK drift failing when the action contract changes.
capabilities.remainingGap: Catalog/get/schema/plan/dry-run, dynamic validate/apply, durable run start/list/get/events/cancel, logs, revert-eligibility/revert, optional branchId planning/apply, and branch object/diff reads have typed TS/browser SDK surfaces. The browser OSDK falls back from static generated descriptors to the same generic governed endpoints, so a newly activated Action is executable immediately without SDK regeneration; sync and async runs share one public history ledger and explicit run-read permission. Python covers the same lifecycle and the separately installable package adds fingerprinted per-Action TypedDict parameters. Runtime/history and the branch-to-activation browser journey are active. Metrics/limit SDK surfaces and external package registry publication remain incomplete.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: A visual Action Type builder, sectioned runtime form auto-rendered from the canonical schema (conditional visibility/default/required, object/interface picker, struct/media/attachment input, permission-aware dropdown, validation, inline-edit eligibility, dry-run impact preview, idempotent submit, version-conflict handling), action history, and monitoring view.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: apps/foundry/src/features/actions renders scalar apply/batch/validate forms consuming the SDK react hooks; Workshop RuntimeActionForm consumes the same SDK.
capabilities.targetBehavior: Builder + sectioned runtime form + history/monitoring that render from the canonical v3 schema, support upload and inline-edit constraints, and preview a real dry-run EditPlan.
capabilities.remainingGap: The branch-first browser Builder authors typed parameters including nested structs, visual sections, defaults/overrides/criteria, ordered object/link and Interface rules, version-pinned functions, registered effects, derived risk, mandatory Action Log, and explicit revert policy. The runtime form uploads media/attachments with visible progress and scan evidence before submission. The same browser journey saves on a branch, submits a proposal, has an assigned human reviewer approve and activate it (the author may self-review), dynamically executes the new Action without SDK regeneration, renders a redacted per-clause criteria decision, reads its normalized log, and reverts it. Object Explorer exposes compiler-approved single-cell Actions only and the browser proves branch activation, inline submission, dynamic Action execution and object reload. The runtime tab also proves snapshot/SSE observation, retry/takeover/fencing, receipts, cancellation and monitoring. Dedicated overlay diff UX, compensation authoring and every linked-object/identity criteria variant remain incomplete.

capabilities.palantirBehavior: An Ontology MCP server exposes object-type query and action validate/plan/apply (and approved functions) as MCP tools/resources, authorized by the intersection of application scope and the calling principal's permissions, with high-risk actions gated plan->approval->apply.
capabilities.foundryLiteBaseline: A current partial consumer Ontology MCP server exists alongside the governed branch-first Builder MCP. Its Streamable HTTP and bearer-preserving stdio surfaces project object, Action, and approved function tools through the intersection of the verified principal token, durable OAuth session, application resource grant, and runtime policy; low-risk Actions can run autonomously while higher-risk applies create immutable human-review proposals. Strict lifecycle and typed JSON-RPC IDs, native structured content with execution-error isError, one durable SSE lease, termination 404, POST/GET/DELETE and tool rate limits with audit/outbox, strict JWT Client Credentials, official Python ClientSession plus PostgreSQL live proof, PostgreSQL rate-limit concurrency/RLS, and browser approval execution are active-covered, while external IdP/DCR interoperability, hosted ChatGPT SaaS tenant connectivity, and production cloud secret manager/KMS remain outside the verified baseline.
capabilities.targetBehavior: An MCP server that maps each Action Type to a deterministic tool schema and calls the same action service, enforcing app-scope ∩ principal permission and a plan->approval->apply boundary for high-risk actions.
capabilities.remainingGap: The consumer Streamable HTTP endpoint projects only app-granted object/action/function tools, accepts standard form-encoded Authorization Code + PKCE and managed confidential Client Credentials service principals, intersects principal/token/app/resource permissions, returns native structured content, and starts only autonomous low-risk durable runs. All other applies create one immutable AIP review. The agent gets a read-only approval-status tool but no approval tool; after a human decision, execution reconstructs the original MCP app/client/scope envelope, rechecks the current grant and plan, blocks revoked scope, commits under the reviewer plus application identity, and exposes the resulting synchronous or asynchronous Action run. Developer Console publication is fail-closed until enabled, its visual MCP tab and tenant Hub expose bounded discovery, app-level Origin policy is enforced, query functions expose version-pinned typed schemas, a bearer-preserving stdio proxy reuses the HTTP boundary, and durable DB sessions/events resume from Last-Event-ID and reject reuse after DELETE. Service clients receive a generated secret once; replay hides it, DB rows retain only vault version coordinates, and rotate/revoke/deactivate atomically revoke durable OAuth access sessions. Every MCP request intersects the token with the online session, while client-credentials issuance locks the client row so rotation cannot race a stale secret into a live token. JSON-RPC replay/conflict and hidden-resource denial are tested. A browser proves MCP request -> immutable review with application/client/scope/plan/version/risk evidence -> human assign/approve/execute -> the same Action run returned through MCP. The live gate uses the official Python MCP ClientSession against a separate Uvicorn process and real PostgreSQL to prove production-object discovery and high-risk approval routing. Production cloud secret manager/KMS and a hosted ChatGPT SaaS tenant connection remain incomplete, so this stays partial.
